title: Quarter-Wave Initialized 12L with Weighted Center Wavelength
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses at exact quarter-wave optical thickness (d = lambda_0/4n) using a weighted center wavelength between the two bands, with all thicknesses explicitly projected above 80 nm, will provide a better optimization starting point than uniform or median initialization, enabling the gradient optimizer to achieve target_score > 0.9968 with improved robustness.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks provide predictable interference minima; initializing near these physical resonances reduces optimization search space and avoids local minima far from physically meaningful solutions.
proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Silicon (12 finite layers, alternating high-low starting with high-index)
soft_objectives: maximize target_score (mean transmittance across both bands)
keep all thicknesses within 20-400 nm bounds
manufacturing_considerations: all layers must be >= 20 nm for deposition control
all layers must be <= 400 nm for stress management
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness d = lambda_0/(4*n) creates destructive interference for reflected waves at design wavelength
Multi-layer AR coatings require thickness tuning away from exact quarter-wave to broaden bandwidth across disjoint bands
expected_advantages: Better initialization reduces optimization iterations to convergence
Quarter-wave starting point is physically meaningful, not arbitrary
Explicit 80 nm floor avoids lower-bound clipping artifacts
known_risks: Exact quarter-wave may not be optimal for dual-band; optimizer must still tune away from initialization
Weighted center wavelength choice may favor one band over the other
execution_request_english: Optimize a 12-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 antireflection stack on silicon substrate for normal-incidence unpolarized illumination. Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness formula d = lambda_0/(4*n) where lambda_0 = 1380 nm (weighted center between 1260-1360 nm and 1530-1565 nm bands), then explicitly project all thicknesses to be >= 80 nm before optimization begins. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with step-size multiplier reduced to 0.5x compared to standard settings. Optimize for mean transmittance across both wavelength bands [1260-1360 nm, 1530-1565 nm]. Layer sequence: Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2 (12 finite layers total). Thickness bounds: 20-400 nm per layer. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization unpolarized. wavelength intervals 1260-1360 nm, 1530-1565 nm. soft objectives: low average reflectance in 1260-1360 nm band; low average reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the specified bands. manufacturing constraints: maximum 12 layers; individual layer thickness between 20 nm and 400 nm; materials restricted to Ta2O5 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Following insight appendage directive: reinitialize with quarter-wave targets projected above 80 nm, reduce optimizer step-size by 50% to enable micro-refinements in sensitive outer layers after global topology is established.
